brief.caption: Proof of work isn't a flaw to fix. It's the reason Bitcoin works. The energy and computation are what make the network impossible to cheat.
brief.headline: Not a flaw. The reason it works.
brief.purpose: Reframe proof of work as a core feature of Bitcoin rather than a wasteful flaw.
brief.visual_direction: Type treatment only. Two stacked lines: 'a flaw' in thin gray type with a single strikethrough, 'the reason it works' in bold Relai orange beneath it. Generous white space around the lines. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: The original PoW explainer was one of the archive's stronger performers; kept the core educational idea and dropped the direct crypto comparison.
suggestions.text:
Proof of work isn't a flaw to fix.
It's the reason Bitcoin works.

brief.caption: No one controls Bitcoin. Everyone controls their own Bitcoin. That's what makes it different from every system before it.
brief.headline: No one controls Bitcoin. Everyone controls their own.
brief.purpose: Highlight Bitcoin's decentralized control structure in one clean contrast.
brief.visual_direction: Comparison of two short phrases side by side, divided by a single thin vertical line. 'no one' in gray on the left, 'everyone' in Relai orange on the right. No icons, type only. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: This line's rhythm and self-custody logic drew solid engagement in the original post.
suggestions.text:
No one controls Bitcoin.
Everyone controls their own Bitcoin.

brief.caption: Hold your own keys. That's the whole point of self-custody: no third party between you and your Bitcoin.
brief.headline: Hold your own keys.
brief.purpose: Reinforce the self-custody message with a simple physical metaphor.
brief.visual_direction: Single prop: one physical key photographed on a plain white background, bow of the key tinted Relai orange. Avoid any bank, vault, or lock-box imagery. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: The 'not your keys' line is a recurring high performer; restated with Relai's approved terminology.
suggestions.text:
Hold your own keys.
That's the whole point of self-custody.

brief.caption: The Olympics has gold, silver, and bronze. Maybe it's time for a Bitcoin medal: for whoever played the longest game.
brief.headline: A medal for the longest game.
brief.purpose: Tie Bitcoin's long-term holding culture to a familiar sporting metaphor.
brief.visual_direction: Comparison device: three classic medal circles in flat outline (gold, silver, bronze) in a row, plus a fourth circle filled solid in Relai orange at the end. Flat shapes only, no ribbons or illustration detail. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: Playful long-term framing in the original drew decent likes and reposts relative to its recency.
suggestions.text:
The Olympics has gold, silver, and bronze.
Maybe it's time for a Bitcoin medal: for whoever played the longest game.

brief.caption: How do you tip someone in gold? Asking for a friend.

brief.purpose: Light humor post contrasting Bitcoin's practical utility with gold.
brief.visual_direction: Comparison prop: a photographed small gold bar on the left in grayscale next to a single coin-shaped Bitcoin prop on the right tinted Relai orange, both the same size. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: Lighthearted comparison format performed well and needs no change to stay compliant.
suggestions.text:
How do you tip someone in gold?
Asking for a friend.

brief.caption: You don't change Bitcoin. Bitcoin changes you.
brief.headline: Bitcoin changes you.
brief.purpose: Capture the personal, reflective mindset shift that holding Bitcoin creates.
brief.visual_direction: Type treatment only, single bold centered line. Relai orange applied only to the word 'you'. No supporting graphic. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: One of the stronger reflective lines in the archive, kept nearly verbatim since it was already clean.
suggestions.text:
You don't change Bitcoin.
Bitcoin changes you.

suggestions.text: Still working on convincing your family to hold some Bitcoin?

suggestions.text:
And Satoshi said, let there be Bitcoin.

brief.caption: A bank can freeze your account. Code can't. That is why some people choose to hold their own keys.
brief.headline: A bank can freeze your account. Code can't.
brief.purpose: Explain the concrete reason some people choose self-custody over a bank account.
brief.visual_direction: Comparison of two simple icons divided by a thin vertical line: a padlock over a bank-column icon on the left in gray, an open code-bracket icon on the right in Relai orange. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: self-custody and holding your own keys recur as a core trust theme across the archive's conviction posts
suggestions.text:
A bank can freeze your account. Code can't.
That is why some people choose to hold their own keys.

brief.caption: Twenty one million will always be twenty one million. No vote, no committee, no exception.
brief.headline: 21,000,000. No vote. No exception.
brief.purpose: Reinforce Bitcoin's fixed supply as an unchangeable rule.
brief.visual_direction: Chart device: a single perfectly flat horizontal line drawn in Relai orange across a time axis, capped at the 21,000,000 mark. Minimal axis labels, no other data. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: extends the proof of work vs trust in people theme to Bitcoin's issuance instead of the consensus mechanism
suggestions.text:
Twenty one million will always be twenty one million.
No vote, no committee, no exception.

brief.caption: Every currency before Bitcoin asked you to trust someone. Bitcoin asks you to verify something.
brief.headline: Trust someone. Or verify something.
brief.purpose: Frame Bitcoin's trust model against traditional money as a simple binary idea.
brief.visual_direction: Comparison of two phrases divided by a thin vertical line: 'trust someone' in gray on the left, 'verify something' in bold Relai orange on the right. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: direct descendant of the proof of stake versus proof of work post, reframed around verification
suggestions.text:
Every currency before Bitcoin asked you to trust someone.
Bitcoin asks you to verify something.

brief.caption: Timing the market takes a perfect guess. Buying a little bit, often, just takes a Tuesday. That's the idea behind an auto-invest plan: more sats when prices are lower, without having to guess.
brief.headline: Perfect timing is hard. A Tuesday isn't.
brief.purpose: Show the DCA mechanic as simpler and more realistic than trying to time the market.
brief.visual_direction: Comparison chart: left side shows a jagged erratic line labeled 'timing attempts', right side shows a row of evenly spaced dots on a calendar grid labeled 'small recurring buys', dots rendered in Relai orange. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: gives the recurring zoom out and discipline theme a concrete mechanic instead of an outcome claim
suggestions.text:
Timing the market takes a perfect guess.
Buying a little bit, often, just takes a Tuesday.

brief.caption: Explaining why prices keep rising is easy. Explaining why Bitcoin's supply never changes is harder, and that's exactly the point.
brief.headline: Why prices rise is easy. Why this doesn't is harder.
brief.purpose: Contrast the ease of explaining inflation with the difficulty of explaining Bitcoin's fixed supply.
brief.visual_direction: Chart device: a rising gray line labeled 'prices' next to a flat line labeled '21 million' rendered in Relai orange, both on one simple shared axis with no further numbers. Logo bottom right.

suggestions.rationale: continues the central bank and money printing theme from the archive without any forward price claim
suggestions.text:
Explaining why prices keep rising is easy.
Explaining why nothing changes is harder.

suggestions.text:
